trees.title: A fluid stain under the car
trees.summary: You find a fluid stain under the car after it has been parked — and want to know what it is.
trees.safety: A brake fluid or fuel leak is always a reason not to drive. Whenever in doubt, don't start the engine and get help.

n1.q: Which part under the car do you see the stain?

options.label: Front, near the radiator or the engine
Middle of the car, after driving with the air conditioning on a hot day
Rear, near the fuel tank area

n2.q: What colour and texture is the fluid?

options.label: Completely clear, with no clear smell

n4.q: What colour is the fluid near the wheel?

options.label: Clear to yellowish, oily, near the wheel body
Clear to pinkish, near the front of the steering column

r-ac-condensation.result: Water from AC condensation — a normal occurrence
r-ac-condensation.text: A clear fluid, with no colour and no smell, that collects roughly under the middle of the car after driving with the air conditioning on a hot day, is water condensed in the AC system — a completely normal occurrence.

r-fuel-leak.text: A stain with a sharp fuel smell near the rear fuel tank area is a leak from the fuel system — a real fire risk.
actions: Don't start the engine and don't drive.
Move away from the car, and don't light a flame or a cigarette near it.
Call roadside assistance or the fire service: {{fact:emergency.fire_and_rescue}}.

r-coolant-leak.text: A green, orange or pink, watery stain near the radiator or the front of the car is leaking coolant — from a hose, the radiator, or the water pump.
actions: Check the coolant level before driving any further.
Go to a garage soon; a continuing leak leads to overheating.
For more detail: [[tree:engine-overheating|the engine is overheating]].

r-oil-leak.text: A dark brown to black, oily stain under the engine area indicates an oil leak — from a seal, a filter that isn't tightened properly, or the valve cover.
actions: Check the oil level on the dipstick before driving any further.
Go to a garage; driving with too little oil can destroy the engine.

r-water-condenser.result: Probably harmless water, not a car fluid
r-water-condenser.text: A completely clear fluid, with no colour, smell or oiliness, could simply be AC condensation or leftover rainwater — not a car fluid.
actions: Check again on a dry day, after the car hasn't been driven for a few hours, to make sure there's no new stain.
If the stain reappears every day, it's still worth checking at a garage.

r-trans-fluid.text: A red or pinkish, oily stain near the middle of the car indicates an automatic transmission fluid leak — from a seal, a cooling hose, or the gearbox itself.
actions: Go to a garage soon; a low fluid level in an automatic gearbox can cause serious damage quickly.
Don't continue with long drives before it's checked.

r-oil-leak-rear.result: Suspected oil leak from the rear of the engine or the gearbox
r-oil-leak-rear.text: A dark brown to black stain in the middle-rear of the car can indicate a leak from the rear crankshaft seal or from the gearbox area itself — the exact source needs checking at a garage.
actions: Go to a garage to trace the exact source of the leak.

r-brake-fluid-leak.text: A clear-to-yellowish, oily stain near one of the wheels is brake fluid leaking from a sealed hydraulic system — it can harm braking ability.
actions: Don't drive the car in this state.

r-power-steering-leak.text: A clear-to-pinkish stain near the front of the steering column indicates a hydraulic power steering fluid leak — over time the steering can become very heavy, mainly at low speed.
actions: Check the power steering fluid level.
Go to a garage soon — don't wait until the steering is completely heavy.
